A1.justification: Both complete, readable PDFs describe the same SketchDNN work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendix A.1–A.4 support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original SketchGraphs experiments, including generation quality, negative log-likelihood, and ablation results in Tables 1–2.

after.justification: v2 retains the original SketchDNN experiments and ablations in Tables 1–2, together with generated examples and failure cases.

M1.justification: The joint continuous-discrete diffusion, transformer architecture, variance schedule, masking, and inference procedure are retained. Expanded loss notation and prediction-target explanations clarify the existing method without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate unconditional generation of CAD sketches containing 8–16 primitives from SketchGraphs. No dataset, task, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Vitruvion, SketchGen, and the positional-encoding and categorical variants. Table 2 retains Vitruvion, latent diffusion, and those same variants. Comparator membership is unchanged within each comparison.

E3.justification: Both retain the preprocessing, 90/5/5 split, training settings, 70K-sketch NLL evaluation, and 10K-sketch image-metric evaluation. Replacing x with t in the loss cutoff corrects notation: the existing prose already specifies timestep-dependent weighting, and the cutoff remains 150.

E4.justification: The positional-encoding, categorical-diffusion, and latent-diffusion ablations are unchanged. Figure 2 retains the variance-schedule analysis, and Section 6.3 retains the same three failure cases and examples.

E5.justification: Tables 1–2 retain single point estimates, and Figure 2 retains its 100,000-sample Monte Carlo calculation. Neither version reports repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–2 and the qualitative examples are retained. For example, SketchDNN remains at 81.33 bits/sketch and FID 7.80, while Vitruvion remains at 84.80 and 16.04, respectively.

T1.justification: Equation (4) changes the density prefactor from product(y_i)/Z(sigma) to product(y_i^-1)/Z(sigma), correcting its inconsistency with the reciprocal factor already derived in Appendix A.2. The appendix derivations and proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about data-space CAD diffusion, Gaussian-Softmax diffusion, superposition, permutation invariance, and state-of-the-art generation performance.

C2.justification: Both attribute the main gains to superposition and a smaller benefit to permutation-invariant denoising. The primitive-only scope, failure explanations, proposed mitigations, and future-work directions are unchanged.

D1.justification: Architecture dimensions, hyperparameters, training budget, hardware, preprocessing, and masking instructions are unchanged. Explicit prediction/target arguments in the loss restate the existing reconstruction setup rather than disclose new implementation or access information.

R1.justification: Section 7 and the reference list retain the same works and positioning, including distinctions from earlier simplex-diffusion methods. Their movement across pages introduces no substantive related-work revision.

P1.justification: v2 corrects misspellings of Gaussian-Softmax and Multinomial, clarifies clean-target prediction, and makes the loss arguments and timestep notation explicit. These are localized edits; the section sequence and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 4 moves from page 8 to page 9, repositioning Figure 5 and reflowing surrounding text and references. Figure content and captions are retained, with no figures or tables added or removed.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects the main-text density to agree with the existing appendix derivation and clarifies the prediction targets and timestep-dependent loss. These changes modestly improve mathematical consistency and readability; the method, empirical evidence, and conclusions remain unchanged.
